article.title: Postman Says It Is Reverting Automatic Claude Code and Codex Plugin Installs; Its Plugin Repo Later Dropped the Installer's Codex Hook Approval
article.summary: A GitHub report says Postman's desktop app installed plugins into Claude Code and Codex on launch. A Postman account said on November 5 it is reverting the change, and the plugin repo later merged a Codex hook change.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

A [GitHub issue](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-app-support/issues/14370) opened on October 25 by a user named indicava reports that opening the Postman desktop app on macOS was followed by installs of Postman plugins into the Claude Code and OpenAI Codex coding agents. [The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io/postman-plugin-coding-agents/) reports that the developer says they had not explicitly authorized these changes. On November 5, a comment on the issue from the account preethammavin said: "In the meantime, we are reverting this change." Both The New Stack and [Notebookcheck](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Postman-added-itself-to-Claude-Code-and-Codex-without-asking.1442933.0.html) reported on the issue. The Herald's contributor model is built by Anthropic, the developer of Claude Code.

## What the report documented

According to the [issue](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-app-support/issues/14370), Postman's own log on the reporter's Mac, running Postman desktop 12.33.4, recorded at 2026-10-24T09:34:14.418Z (UTC) an install whose source was `auto-existing-upgrade`, with the results `claude-code:installed` and `codex:installed`. In Codex's configuration the reporter found a Postman plugin marketplace, an enabled Postman plugin and a `trusted_hash` entry for a session-start hook. In Claude Code, `postman@claude-plugins-official` was enabled in `settings.json`, and a Postman executable had appeared in `~/.local/bin`.

The issue says the hook tells Codex to load Postman's `postman:api-engineer` skill before responding to any non-trivial API engineering task, and that the plugin also configured a connection to Postman's remote MCP server, which failed in Codex with an "Auth required" error. The reporter pointed to the installer source, where `installer/src/hosts/codex.ts` calls `approvePostmanHook` after installing the plugin, and wrote that the trust record alone "does not prove who created that specific record".

[The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io/postman-plugin-coding-agents/), citing Postman's own documentation, reported that the installer can automatically approve a session-start hook on the user's behalf, while developers who install the plugin directly through Codex must review and approve the hook themselves. The reporter's issue says it "does not claim to establish data exfiltration". The New Stack says the report provides no evidence that Postman collected or transmitted API data, and [Notebookcheck](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Postman-added-itself-to-Claude-Code-and-Codex-without-asking.1442933.0.html) says there is no evidence that Postman collected data this way.

At the time of The New Stack's November 3 article, the report covered one macOS installation that had not been independently reproduced, and Postman had not responded to the outlet's questions about the installs, hook approvals and user consent.

## Further reports in the thread

A later comment by ronthedrummer, posted at 2026-11-03T23:56:23Z, described a second Mac: the app updated from 12.31.3 to 12.35.1 on launch, and the log showed Claude Code and Codex installed with Cursor recorded as `cursor:already-installed`. In that case, according to the [issue thread](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-app-support/issues/14370), the commenter wrote that `config.toml` had no `hooks.state` or `trusted_hash` entry, and a later comment said he had not run Codex to watch whether the hook printed. In the 12.33.4 report, Codex's configuration did contain a `trusted_hash` entry. The Herald sets the two accounts side by side without reconciling them.

Another commenter, ck-tecso, posted Postman entries from `~/.copilot/settings.json` and wrote that Postman's uninstall menu entry did not remove Postman from Copilot. [Notebookcheck](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Postman-added-itself-to-Claude-Code-and-Codex-without-asking.1442933.0.html), published on November 5, summarizes the thread as users reporting entries in Cursor and the GitHub Copilot CLI as well, and says all reported cases so far involve Macs.

## Postman's response and the plugin repository

The comment from preethammavin was posted at 2026-11-05T03:46:20Z; [Notebookcheck](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Postman-added-itself-to-Claude-Code-and-Codex-without-asking.1442933.0.html) describes its author as a Postman staff member. The comment said the change was intended to "simplify the setup for developers who use agents to build APIs with coding agents" and that Postman "will be re-designing the experience with the right level of control", adding that it is reverting the change in the meantime. [Notebookcheck](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Postman-added-itself-to-Claude-Code-and-Codex-without-asking.1442933.0.html) adds that reverting the change does not remove what is already installed. The [issue](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-app-support/issues/14370) was closed at 11:41:48Z the same day by another account and is locked.

Timestamps below are UTC from GitHub. In the postman-plugin repository, [pull request #147](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/pull/147), opened at 11:55:02Z on November 5, proposed removing the installer's Codex hook auto-approval and was closed unmerged at 17:18:18Z. [Pull request #149](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/pull/149), which supersedes it, was merged at 17:19:08Z. Its [commit message](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/commit/652e42eca1ef27af623fb671d8eee3984295c1f4) says: "The installer wrote trust for Postman's hook into the user's Codex config. The user must make that choice." The [same pull request](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/pull/149) sets the Codex route to declare no session-start hook, so that Codex "still gets every skill and the Postman MCP server" but "no longer gets the session-start mandate".

A [commit reverting that change](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/commit/3d3c68f054543114bb6c58e072538c3b7d3f9401) was made at 23:50:29Z the same day, with no reason in its message. [Pull request #152](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/pull/152) reapplied it and was merged at 2026-11-06T08:26:15Z. [Pull request #148](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/pull/148), merged at 15:06:17Z that day, expands `npx @postman/postman-plugin remove` so that it also removes, among other things, the Codex hook approval and Postman marketplace entries for several agents. [Release pull request #153](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-plugin/pull/153), merged at 15:25:13Z, lists both changes for version 0.8.0 of `@postman/postman-plugin`. The descriptions of these pull requests do not mention the GitHub issue.

## What remains unclear

None of the cited sources states which Postman desktop release carries the revert. The New Stack's page carries a disclosure that its owner, Insight Partners, is an investor in OpenAI and Postman. The Herald's count of independent outlets is two, The New Stack (with the investor tie above) and Notebookcheck; the GitHub thread posts are user reports, not verified findings.
